purpose: Repeat the Step-10B dual-initialization development benchmark with a larger optimization ceiling and crash-safe persistence, while keeping architecture, data mixture, optimizer, selection rule, and gates fixed and evaluating only on a fresh untouched outer cohort.

training.domain_schedule: equal optimizer-block count from original and bridge per epoch; shorter block list cycles deterministically

selection.retention_reference: matching-seed warm-start epoch-0 original-domain selection metrics
eligibility: original mechanism balanced accuracy >= warm-start epoch-0 original mechanism BA - 0.02
original effect balanced accuracy >= warm-start epoch-0 original effect BA - 0.02
eligible_checkpoint_order: minimum(original mechanism BA, bridge mechanism BA)

checkpointing.atomic_protocol: write temp in same directory -> flush -> fsync file -> os.replace -> fsync parent directory

evaluation.seed_aggregation: mean logits across seeds after per-seed checkpoint selection
evaluation.effect_threshold: one threshold per initialization selected from concatenated original+bridge selection logits, then frozen before fresh outer evaluation

original_retention_gate.reference: untouched Step-9A ensemble evaluated on the same fresh original outer cohort

initialization_decision.warm_reuse_preferred_if: warm passes full dual-domain gate and scratch does not show clear superiority
scratch_clear_superiority_requires: scratch and warm both pass full gate
paired bootstrap CI lower for scratch-minus-warm bridge mechanism BA > 0.01
scratch does not worsen original mechanism retention by more than 0.01 relative to warm

scientific_boundaries: No architecture, graph-input-contract, learning-rate, gradient-clipping, batch-size, domain-weight, loss-weight, scheduler, EMA, SWA, or dataset-fit/selection change is introduced in Step 10C.
The only scientific optimization change from Step 10B is max_epochs 20 -> 40; early stopping remains unchanged and may stop runs earlier.
Atomic persistence, exact resume, progress monitoring, wall-time logging, and clipping telemetry are engineering/observability changes only.
The spent Step-10B outer cohorts are not used to select, tune, or evaluate Step 10C.
No QPU execution and no spent confirmatory cohort access occur in Step 10C.
